title.narrative: 2024 - SHF Reserve for Emergencies - SP Health and WASH in SKS

description.narrative: ltpgtWater, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH): ltbrgtThis WASH response will aim at the dissemination of key health and hygiene messages and distribution of WASH and non-food item (NFIs) kits to conflict-affected populations, specifically internally displaced people (IDPs) in South Kordofan State (SKS).nbsp These will increase access to NFIs for 500 households (HHs) or 3,500 crisis-affected people, safeguarding their health and dignity and improving their living conditions, as well as increasing their knowledge to mitigate the spread of WASH-related diseases. Samaritan’s Purse will coordinate closely with the affected populations and community leaders to identify the target population and coordinate these distributions. The NFI distributions will be accompanied by beneficiary sensitization on key health and hygiene messages regarding measures to prevent WASH-related diseases. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtHealth:ltbrgtThe health response will be implemented to decrease morbidity and mortality levels among IDPs in SKS, targeting Western Jebel localities. The health programming will be implemented in close collaboration with the Secretariat of Health (SoH).nbsp The activities will be integrated with WASH activities. The following three main health activities are planned:ltbrgt1. Continue implementing the integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) program in 10 villages where IDPs have been integrated in Western Jebel.ltbrgt2. Distribute 2,000 clean delivery kits (CDKs) to 10 health facilities (HFs) in Western Jebel where IDPs have been integrated. This is aimed at boosting the capacity to conduct clean deliveries with the influx of IDPs.ltbrgt3. Distribute basic malaria medicines to 10 HFs in Western Jebel where IDPs have been integrated. This is aimed at boosting the capacity of health facilities to manage malaria with the influx of IDPs.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtConflict Sensitivity: SKS has been affected by protracted conflict, including intercommunal violence, political tensions, and historical grievances. The complex interplay of ethnic, political and economic dynamics exacerbates competition over land, scarce resources and power. Historical marginalization and perceived injustices fuel grievances among various ethnic groups, contributing to cycles of violence and instability. However, amidst these challenges lie opportunities for social cohesion through community engagement by involving local communities in decision making and program implementation. Integrating health and WASH interventions can promote collaboration and trust among the community members and implementing partners. ltbrgtlt/pgt
